title: A Framework for Approaching AI Education in Educator Preparation Programs
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the gap in artificial intelligence (AI) education resources for educator preparation programs (EPPs). The authors argue that while many professional learning opportunities exist for inservice K-12 educators, preservice teachers and EPP faculty need more structured guidance for integrating AI into teacher preparation and for teaching AI literacy in PreK-12 settings.

The paper proposes a framework of seven critical strategies for systemically embedding AI education into EPPs. These strategies include building a foundational understanding of AI, cultivating skills for using AI instructional tools, using the Five Big Ideas in AI to guide K-12 AI literacy, creating exploratory learning experiences, infusing AI literacy across the curriculum, integrating critical examinations of equity/ethics/cultural responsiveness, and embedding these approaches across teacher preparation programs. The framework explicitly references tools and examples such as Khanmigo, ChatGPT, adaptive tutors, robots, and XR environments, but it is not an empirical evaluation of any one intervention.

The intended population is higher-education educator preparation stakeholders: EPP faculty, preservice teachers, and teacher candidates in the United States. The broader implementation context is teacher preparation coursework and faculty-led professional learning, with implications for future K-12 classrooms. The authors conclude that AI literacy should be treated as a program-wide responsibility rather than a single-course topic, and that further research is needed on faculty and preservice teacher knowledge, curriculum integration, barriers, and the effects of implementing the proposed strategies.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual framework / position paper rather than an empirical study. It does not report a defined sample, design, or measured outcomes for K-12 students or teachers, so there is no evaluative evidence base to rate beyond theory and recommendations.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper is potentially important for implementation guidance, especially around preparation conditions and moderator-like factors such as equity, ethics, faculty capacity, and curricular infusion. However, it provides no direct outcome evidence, so its observed impact is indirect and currently unclear.

interventions.use_case: Framework and implementation guidance for using Khanmigo as an AI-powered pedagogical agent/chatbot in K-12 classrooms, especially for tutoring-style student interactions and teacher preparation for future use.
Mentions ALEKS as an example of an AI system that adapts instruction and assessment to individual learners' needs.
Describes adaptive tutoring and assessment systems more generally as personalized instruction tools that tailor support to learners' strengths and weaknesses.
Uses generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and Midjourney in the context of prompt engineering and AI literacy, with some discussion of text-generation and media creation.
